title: Privileged Role Rotation and Certification Guideline
author: Claire Chen
content:
Summary
This guideline defines the standard process for certification and rotation of privileged roles and service principals across Redwood Inference. It ties RBAC review cadence, privileged credential rotation, audit logging requirements, evidence collection, and exceptions handling into a single operational playbook that satisfies SOC-like audit expectations and internal security controls.

Purpose
- Reduce risk surface by ensuring privileges are reviewed on a regular cadence.
- Ensure auditability: each role change and certification must produce verifiable evidence stored in the compliance evidence store.
- Provide a repeatable, minimally disruptive rotation and emergency remediation process.

Scope
Applies to:
- Human privileged roles (admin, infra-admin, billing-admin, model-onboarder)
- Machine/service principals with elevated permissions (k8s-cluster-admin, kube-ops-bot, model-deployer-sa)
- Cross-account/third-party roles we manage for partner integrations
Excludes: ephemeral developer feature flags limited to single-day access (see Exceptions).

Definitions
- Privileged Role: A role granting write or admin-level access to production systems or access to customer data.
- Certification: Formal attestation by the role owner or approver that the role membership is correct.
- Rotation: Replacement of credentials (password, key, token) or reassignment of membership to align with least privilege.
- Evidence Bundle: A timestamped set of artifacts (certification log entry, approver name, audit export, rotation change record) stored in the compliance evidence bucket.

Owners & Accountability
- Security (Role & Access Team): overall process owner; runs quarterly certification campaigns and maintains automation.
- Service/Platform Teams: owners of roles created by the team; responsible for certifying membership and executing rotation steps.
- IAM Admins: perform technical rotations for managed identities and service principals.
- Audit/Compliance: retain evidence and review certification completeness prior to audits.

Certification Cadence (Table)
- Human high-privilege roles (SRE, infra-admin): quarterly
- Human medium-privilege roles (product-admin, billing): semi-annually
- Service principals with 'write' access: quarterly
- Long-lived keys (>90 days): immediate rotation policy; should not be used except with documented exception
- Short-lived tokens (<=24h): no certification required beyond normal onboarding/offboarding verification

Procedures
1) Quarterly Certification Campaign (standard flow)
   1. Security triggers campaign via AccessCert tool on Day 0 and notifies role owners.
   2. Role owners receive an email with a link to the certification portal and a CSV export of current members.
   3. Role owners perform one of: 
      - Confirm members are correct -> click "certify" with free-text justification if no changes
      - Remove stale members -> certify after update
      - Escalate uncertainty -> assign to an approver with a 7-day SLA
   4. If any role is uncertified after 14 days, Security opens a remediation ticket and notifies people managers; unresolved >30 days triggers automatic temporary suspension of role membership pending manual review.

2) Privileged Credential Rotation (routine)
   - Service principals: rotate keys/tokens every 90 days by default. Managed identity recommended where supported.
   - Human credentials: enforce password rotation per company policy (People Ops) and require MFA; do not use long-lived CLI keys.
   - Kubernetes cluster admin tokens: replace scheduled token each 30 days for operators; kubeconfig with short-lived impersonation recommended.

3) Emergency Rotation (incident-driven)
   - Trigger: suspected credential compromise, privilege escalation, or confirmed audit anomaly.
   - Steps:
     a. Incident commander assigns an Access Responder (AR).
     b. AR identifies affected roles/service principals and marks them in the incident tracker.
     c. AR issues an immediate rotation plan: revoke bearer tokens, rotate service principal secrets, scale down ephemeral credentials, and apply deny-lists where available.
     d. AR documents all revocations and new credentials in the Evidence Bundle and marks retention tags.

Audit Logging Requirements
- All role membership changes, role creation/deletion, and credential rotations must be written to the centralized audit log stream with the following required fields: timestamp, actor (user/service), resource (role/identity), change_type (add/remove/rotate), justification, ticket_id.
- Audit logs must be immutable for 365 days for production-critical roles and 730 days for roles that touch regulated data.
- Example log format (JSON line):
```
{
  "ts": "2025-03-18T14:32:11Z",
  "actor": "samir.patel@redwood.com",
  "resource": "k8s:cluster-admin",
  "change_type": "remove",
  "justification": "role recertification - user moved to contractor org",
  "ticket_id": "AC-2025-0123"
}
```

Evidence & Storage
- Evidence Bundle must include: certification portal export (CSV), approver attestation (name + timestamp), audit log slice (ndjson), rotation change record (commit/ticket), and any supporting emails.
- Storage location: s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/privileged-certifications/YYYY/MM/
- Retention policy: evidence for privileged roles retained for 7 years for enterprise customers with regulated data; default retention 3 years for non-regulated products.
- Encryption: objects must be encrypted with customer key when tied to customer data or with the company KMS key otherwise.

Automation & Tooling
- AccessCert: primary tool used for certification campaigns. It exposes a CLI and API used by Security and platform teams.
- Example CLI command to export current binding for role `infra-admin`:
```
accesscert export-bindings --role infra-admin --format csv > infra-admin-members.csv
```
- Example API call to trigger a campaign (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://accesscert.internal.redwood.com/api/v1/campaigns \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN' \
 -d '{"roles":["infra-admin","k8s-cluster-admin"],"due_days":14}'
```
- Audit extraction snippet (example SQL-like query against the audit store):
```
SELECT ts, actor, resource, change_type, ticket_id FROM audit_events 
WHERE resource LIKE 'rbac:%' AND ts >= '2024-12-01' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 5000;
```

Exceptions and Risk Acceptance
- Short-lived, one-off elevated access for on-call debugging may be approved for up to 24 hours without formal certification if logged to the audit stream with justification.
- Any long-lived exception (>90 days) requires Risk & Exceptions submission with a compensating controls checklist and Exec Security approval; all approved exceptions must have an owner and expiration date.

Reporting & Metrics
- KPIs tracked by Security:
  - Percentage of privileged roles certified on schedule (target >= 95% per quarter)
  - Mean time to remediate uncertified role after campaign close (target < 7 days)
  - Number of emergency rotations per quarter (trend analysis)
  - Fraction of evidence bundles complete at time of certification (target >= 100%)

Incident Response Integration
- When an incident is opened with a potential auth compromise, the incident commander references this guideline to:
  - rapidly identify impacted roles via the role-index;
  - trigger emergency rotation flow;
  - enrich incident timeline with audit log slices and evidence bundles.
- Post-incident: Security runs a targeted re-certification campaign for impacted role owners and mandates a forensics audit on rotation artifacts.

Appendices
A. Sample Certification Email (send from AccessCert)
Subject: Action required: Quarterly Certification for role `infra-admin`
Body: Please review the attached list of members for `infra-admin`. Confirm membership or remove stale entries by 2025-04-02. Failure to certify will result in automatic suspension per company policy.

B. Example Evidence Checklist
- CSV export of members [yes/no]
- Approver attestation (name + timestamp) [yes/no]
- Audit log export covering change window [yes/no]
- Rotation ticket/PR link [yes/no]
- Artifact stored at s3 path [s3://redwood-compliance/evidence/privileged-certifications/YYYY/MM/]

C. Quick reference: Role classification and recommended cadence
- admin / infra-admin / cluster-admin: quarterly
- billing-admin / payments: semi-annual
- analytics-service-principal (read-only): annual

Change History
- 2024-11-12: Created by Claire Chen.
- 2025-01-08: Clarified emergency rotation steps (reviewer: Samir Patel).
- 2025-03-18: Updated retention to 7 years for regulated-customer evidence; tightened audit log immutability windows.

Contact
For process questions, contact the Role & Access Team at access-team@redwood.com or open a ticket in #security-ops.
